newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canada's Calliope plans to list in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Calliope plans to list in Australia.

text.p: Vancouver-listed Calliope Metals Corp said on Wednesday it will offer 11 million shares at 95 Australian cents each as a prelude to listing on the Australian Stock Exchange.

In a statement made in Vancouver and issued here, Calliope said it had reached agreement with Australian stockbroker Wilson HTM Corporate Services Ltd for a firm underwriting of the issue, subject to regulatory approval.
Calliope is studying the development of a nickel/cobalt ore processing facility at Gladstone in Queensland.
Net proceeds of the issue and a Canadian special warrant financing is estimated to total about C$13.65 million, it said.
The funds will be used to accelerate project development, to identify and test laterite deposits for possible acquisition and to add to working capital, Calliope said.
It said it commissioned Kvaerner John Brown Pty Ltd to conduct the final feasibility study, currently under way, for the Gladstone facility.

Calliope said it planned to use the Sherritt International Consultants Inc's established pressure acid leach technology to process 1.2 million tonnes dry weight a year of lateritic ore to be purchased from established New Caledonian mining companies.
Planned annual production is 18,740 tonnes of nickel and 1,890 tonnes of cobalt in a mixed sulphide product.
"The company is proceeding on schedule towards finalising the detailed engineering study by May 1997," Calliope chairman Peter Matheson said in the statement.

Calliope said Wilson HTM, as underwriter, would receive a selling commission and underwriting fee totalling six percent and a broker's option comprising 10 percent of the shares underwritten, exerciseable at A$1.20 each until September 10, 1998.
